It is known that various coral species are able to photoacclimatize when living at greater depths (Chalker et al., 1988). As a response to the reduced light levels deep water corals often have increased levels of pigments in their tissue (Porter et al., 1984; Battey and Porter, 1988). A further indication of lack of photoacclimatization in P. astreoides and S. michelinii is the lack of a decrease in the chlorophyll a /c 2 ratio with depth. Chlorophyll c 2 is much more efficient in absorbing the blue light available at greater depths.
